- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price drops, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 7–10 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been above 70.00 for 5+ days, model often fails to revert; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) correlate with model overconfidence; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days after sentiment peak.
